title: Longitudinal quantification of mouse gastric tumor organoid viability and growth using luminescence and microscopy
protocol: Manually count the number of organoids in each well of a 24-well tissue culture plate under a bright field microscope and record the total number of organoids observed.
Aspirate and discard Organoid Growth Media from each well.
Add 1 mL of 4°C cold Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent to each dome.
Gently pipette Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent onto each dome 10 times using a 1,000 μL pipette tip to break the organoids into smaller fragments.
Pool the suspension from each well into a 15 mL conical tube after disruption.
Rinse each well with 1 mL of 4°C cold Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent and add this to the same 15 mL conical tube.
Place the tube on an orbital roller at room temperature for 10 min.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 × g at 4°C for 5 min using a swinging bucket rotor centrifuge.
Carefully aspirate and discard the supernatant without disturbing the organoid pellet.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in 5 mL of cold Wash Media.
Centrifuge at 400 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant without disrupting the organoid pellet.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in 1 mL of cold Wash Media.
Transfer the resuspended organoid pellet into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 9,600 × g at 4°C for 5 min using a benchtop mini/micro fixed angle rotor centrifuge.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant without disrupting the organoid pellet.
Gently resuspend the pellet in ice cold Basement Membrane Matrix.
Resuspend organoids in Basement Membrane Matrix on ice.
Plate 35 μL of the resuspended organoid mixture into each well of a white, opaque-walled, clear-bottomed 96-well tissue culture plate.
Mix gently by pipetting after plating every 5 wells to ensure even distribution.
Maintain microcentrifuge tubes containing organoids on ice throughout the procedure.
Keep the assay plate on ice in a Class II biological safety cabinet during setup.
Ensure the plate is level.
Dispense 35 μL of the organoid Basement Membrane Matrix mix directly into the center of each well.
Include three blank wells containing only Basement Membrane Matrix and Organoid Growth Media.
Place the white, opaque-walled, clear-bottomed 96-well tissue culture plate into a 37°C incubator with 10% CO2.
Incubate for 15 min to solidify the organoid Basement Membrane Matrix.
Prepare Assay Media during the 15 min incubation period.
Equilibrate NanoLuc® Enzyme (1000×) reagent to 37°C in an incubator for approximately 10 minutes or until thawed.
Equilibrate MT Cell Viability Substrate (1000×) reagent to 37°C in an incubator for approximately 10 minutes or until thawed.
Prepare the Assay Media by adding NanoLuc® Enzyme and MT Cell Viability Substrate to Organoid Growth Media at a final concentration of 1×.
Add 100 μL of Assay Media to each well in a Class II biological safety cabinet.
Return the plated organoids to a 37°C, 10% CO2 incubator for at least 16 hours. Preferably allow for 24 hours to establish the organoids.
Measure luminescence using a plate reading luminometer with an integration time of 0.25 seconds to 1 second.
Protect the assay from direct light to reduce degradation of the RealTime-Glo™ MT Cell Viability Substrate.
Maintain the assay at 37°C when measuring luminescence.
Use a luminometer with temperature control if available.
Measure lumenscence immediately after removing the assay from the 37°C incubator if a controlled temperature luminometer is unavailable.
Conduct measurements in a Class II biological safety cabinet to maintain sterility.
Image organoids for quantification of diameter as a surrogate measure of growth.
Determine whether reduced luminescence signals are due to senescence or death.
Take photomicrographs of each well immediately after measuring luminescence.
Pre-heat the stage incubator of an IX81 Olympus inverted microscope to 37°C with 10% CO2.
Determine upper and lower z-stack limits and associated step sizes for the assay.
Use a z-stack involving 10 steps spaced ∼50 μm apart.
Acquire multiple photos of each well per time point based on the number of z-stack step sizes used.
Protect the assay from direct light to reduce degradation of the RealTime-Glo™ MT Cell Viability Substrate.
Secure the assay plate to the microscope stage for imaging.
Take full-well photomicrographs of each organoid well with suitable upper and lower z-stack limits and associated step sizes.
Return the assay to a 37°C, 10% CO2 incubator after imaging is complete.
Dilute desired concentrations of test compound(s) at 2× in Assay Media.
Overlay 100 μL of diluted test compound(s) to the pre-existing 100 μL per well to make a 1× concentration.
Return the assay to the incubator and remove only when measuring viability and imaging organoids at desired time points.
Quantify organoid viability by luminescence.
Measure the metabolic activity of viable organoids using the RealTime-Glo™ MT Cell Viability Assay.
Express the amount of luminescence signal measured by a luminometer in Relative Light Units (RLUs).
Calculate the average RLU from technical triplicates for blank wells and each experimental condition.
Subtract the average RLU of blank wells from the average RLU of each experimental condition to determine corrected RLUs.
Calculate fold change in viability across different time points by dividing the corrected RLU of each time point by the corrected RLU of the first time point.
Quantify organoid growth by microscopy.
Capture photomicrographs of each well using an Olympus IX81 microscope.
Draw a line across each organoid at each time point to quantify growth.
Measure the diameter of each organoid using the Measure function in OlyVIA image software.
Repeat the measurement until the diameter of every organoid is determined.
Measure only organoids that are in focus.
Identify the clearest image of each organoid in a z-stack for quantification.
Calculate the organoid diameter range by subtracting the smallest from the largest organoid diameter at Day 0.
Divide the calculated value by 3 to determine the diameter range for small, medium, and large organoids.
Assign each organoid into either small, medium, or large groups based on the calculated ranges.
Calculate the percentage of each organoid size at each time point by dividing the number of small, medium, or large organoids by the total number of organoids counted per well.
